CAST.summary: Convert to a type; errors on failure (use TRY_CAST instead)

CONVERT.summary: Convert type; style formats dates/numbers; type goes first

TRY_CONVERT.summary: Like CONVERT but returns NULL on failure instead of an error

ISNULL.summary: Second arg if first is NULL; typed as first, may truncate

COALESCE.summary: First non-NULL arg; highest-precedence type, no truncation

NULLIF.summary: NULL if both are equal, else the first; turns 0 into NULL
NULLIF.example: SELECT 10 / NULLIF(0, 0)   -- NULL, won't throw division by zero

IIF.summary: Two-branch CASE; returns second arg if true, third if false

DATEADD.summary: Add an interval to a date; datepart is unquoted (DAY, MONTH)
DATEADD.example: SELECT DATEADD(DAY, -14, GETDATE())   -- Same time two weeks ago

DATEDIFF.summary: Counts datepart boundaries crossed, not elapsed time

DATEPART.summary: Extract date part as integer; use DATENAME for text

EOMONTH.summary: Last day of the month; optional arg adds months first

FORMAT.summary: Format via .NET string; uses CLR, much slower than CONVERT

CHARINDEX.summary: Position of first substring, 1-based; 0 if not found

SUBSTRING.summary: Substring from start for length chars; no error past the end

LEN.summary: Character count excluding trailing spaces; bytes: DATALENGTH

STRING_AGG.summary: Concatenate group values; order with WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY)

ROW_NUMBER.summary: Sequential number per OVER order, no ties; ORDER BY required

NVARCHAR.example: DECLARE @title nvarchar(200)   -- Default 1 when length omitted, MAX can hold 2 GB

VARCHAR.example: DECLARE @code varchar(20)   -- Characters limited by collation; use NVARCHAR

DECIMAL.example: DECLARE @amount decimal(18, 2)   -- 18 total digits, 2 decimal places

DATETIME2.example: DECLARE @at datetime2(3)   -- Parentheses are fractional second precision, default 7

BIT.example: DECLARE @isActive bit = 1   -- Strings 'TRUE'/'FALSE' can also be converted

UNIQUEIDENTIFIER.example: DECLARE @id uniqueidentifier = NEWID()   -- Clustered key causes splits

DATENAME.summary: Extract date part as text; result varies by language setting
DATENAME.example: SELECT DATENAME(MONTH, '2026-09-08')   -- 09 (September when language is English)

AVG.summary: Average, ignoring NULL; integer columns truncate the result
AVG.example: SELECT AVG(CAST(CopyNo AS decimal(9, 2))) FROM dbo.Cat_BookCopy   -- Cast for decimals

CHECKSUM_AGG.summary: Checksum of integer values in group to detect data changes
CHECKSUM_AGG.example: SELECT CHECKSUM_AGG(CHECKSUM(CopyNo)) FROM dbo.Cat_BookCopy   -- Changes with any value

COUNT.summary: Row count; COUNT(*) includes NULL, COUNT(col) excludes NULL
COUNT.example: SELECT COUNT(*), COUNT(ReturnDate) FROM dbo.Loan   -- Second excludes NULL

COUNT_BIG.summary: Like COUNT but returns bigint, for over 2.1 billion rows
COUNT_BIG.example: SELECT COUNT_BIG(*) FROM dbo.LoanDetail   -- COUNT would overflow here

GROUPING.summary: 1 for ROLLUP-added rows, 0 for actual NULL values
GROUPING.example: SELECT GROUPING(BranchId) FROM dbo.Loan GROUP BY ROLLUP(BranchId)   -- Subtotal rows are 1

GROUPING_ID.summary: Combines GROUPING bits into one int for the subtotal level
GROUPING_ID.example: SELECT GROUPING_ID(BranchId) FROM dbo.Loan GROUP BY ROLLUP(BranchId)   -- 1 for totals

MAX.summary: Maximum, ignoring NULL; strings compare by collation
MAX.example: SELECT MAX(LoanDate) FROM dbo.Loan   -- Most recent loan date

MIN.summary: Minimum, ignoring NULL; NULL if every value is NULL
MIN.example: SELECT MIN(LoanDate) FROM dbo.Loan   -- First loan date

STDEV.summary: Sample standard deviation; population version is STDEVP
STDEV.example: SELECT STDEV(CopyNo) FROM dbo.Cat_BookCopy   -- Returns NULL with only one row

STDEVP.summary: Population standard deviation (divides by N); sample: STDEV
STDEVP.example: SELECT STDEVP(CopyNo) FROM dbo.Cat_BookCopy   -- Returns 0 with only one row

SUM.summary: Total, ignoring NULL; NULL (not 0) when there are no rows
SUM.example: SELECT ISNULL(SUM(Quantity), 0) FROM dbo.LoanDetail   -- Returns 0 when no data

VAR.example: SELECT VAR(CopyNo) FROM dbo.Cat_BookCopy   -- Returns NULL with only one row

VARP.summary: Population variance (divides by N); sample: VAR
VARP.example: SELECT VARP(CopyNo) FROM dbo.Cat_BookCopy   -- Returns 0 with only one row

DENSE_RANK.summary: Ties share a rank, no gaps after; for gaps use RANK

FIRST_VALUE.summary: First value in the frame; default frame ends at current row
FIRST_VALUE.example: SELECT FIRST_VALUE(CopyNo) OVER (ORDER BY LoanDate) FROM dbo.Loan   -- Earliest

LAG.summary: Value from N rows back; third arg (default NULL) if none
LAG.example: SELECT LAG(LoanDate, 1) OVER (ORDER BY LoanDate) FROM dbo.Loan   -- Previous loan date

LAST_VALUE.summary: Last value in the frame; default frame ends at current row
LAST_VALUE.example: SELECT LAST_VALUE(CopyNo) OVER (ORDER BY LoanDate) FROM dbo.Loan   -- Defaults to current

LEAD.summary: Value from N rows ahead; third arg (default NULL) if none
LEAD.example: SELECT LEAD(LoanDate, 1) OVER (ORDER BY LoanDate) FROM dbo.Loan   -- Next loan date

NTILE.summary: Split ordered rows into N groups; earlier groups get extras
NTILE.example: SELECT NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY LoanDate) FROM dbo.Loan   -- Quartiles 1 to 4

RANK.summary: Ties share a rank, gaps after; for no gaps use DENSE_RANK

ASCII.summary: ASCII code of first char; UNICODE for Unicode

CHAR.summary: Character for code 0-255; NULL if out of range
CHAR.example: SELECT CHAR(13) + CHAR(10)   -- Line break; use NCHAR for Unicode code points

CONCAT.summary: Concatenate 2+ values; NULL counts as an empty string

CONCAT_WS.summary: Concatenate with separator; skips NULL and their separators

DATALENGTH.summary: Bytes used, including trailing spaces; characters: LEN

DIFFERENCE.summary: SOUNDEX similarity of two strings, 0 to 4; English only

LEFT.summary: Leftmost N chars; whole string if N exceeds its length

LTRIM.summary: Remove leading spaces; SQL Server 2022+ can take characters

NCHAR.summary: Unicode character; accepts larger range than CHAR

PATINDEX.summary: First pattern match position 1-based; 0 if not found

QUOTENAME.summary: Wrap as a valid identifier; escapes ] for dynamic SQL

REPLACE.summary: Replace all occurrences; comparison affected by collation

REPLICATE.summary: Repeat string count times; NULL if count negative

REVERSE.summary: Reverse string; surrogate pairs and combining chars break

RIGHT.summary: Rightmost N chars; often paired with REPLICATE for padding

RTRIM.summary: Remove trailing spaces; LEN ignores them, DATALENGTH doesn't

SOUNDEX.summary: 4-char English phonetic code; meaningless for other text

SPACE.summary: String of N spaces; for more than 8000 use REPLICATE

STR.summary: Number to right-aligned string; rounds decimals, pads spaces

STRING_SPLIT.summary: Split a string into rows; separator is a single character
STRING_SPLIT.example: SELECT value FROM STRING_SPLIT('A,B,C', ',')   -- Three rows: A, B, C

STUFF.summary: Delete length chars from start, insert new; start is 1-based

TRANSLATE.summary: Map source chars to replacement 1-to-1; lists same length

TRIM.summary: Remove leading and trailing spaces; like LTRIM(RTRIM(x))

UNICODE.summary: Code point of the first character; prefix literals with N

UPPER.summary: Uppercase; only affects characters that have case

DATEFROMPARTS.summary: Assemble date from year/month/day; fails if invalid date
DATEFROMPARTS.example: SELECT DATEFROMPARTS(2026, 2, 30)   -- Error: February does not have 30 days

DAY.summary: Extracts day, equals DATEPART(DAY, date), returns integer

GETDATE.summary: Current local time as datetime; precision ~3.33ms

GETUTCDATE.summary: Current UTC time as datetime; no time zone offset

ISDATE.summary: 1 if string converts to date; varies by language/DATEFORMAT

MONTH.summary: Month number, same as DATEPART(MONTH, date); name: DATENAME

SWITCHOFFSET.summary: Convert to different time zone offset; time point unchanged
SWITCHOFFSET.example: SELECT SWITCHOFFSET(SYSDATETIMEOFFSET(), '+08:00')   -- Same instant in Taipei time

SYSDATETIME.summary: Current local time as datetime2(7); far more precise

SYSDATETIMEOFFSET.summary: Current time with zone offset as datetimeoffset(7)

SYSUTCDATETIME.summary: Current UTC time as datetime2(7) for cross-zone storage

TODATETIMEOFFSET.summary: Attach a time zone offset; the clock time is unchanged
TODATETIMEOFFSET.example: SELECT TODATETIMEOFFSET(SYSDATETIME(), '+08:00')   -- Time unchanged, zone added

YEAR.summary: Extracts year, equals DATEPART(YEAR, date), returns integer

ABS.summary: Absolute value; typed as the arg; min negative overflows

CEILING.summary: Smallest integer >= the value; return type unchanged

EXP.summary: E to power of number returns float; inverse is LOG

FLOOR.summary: Round down to integer; negative numbers round more negative

LOG.summary: Natural logarithm; second arg specifies base, must be > 0

POWER.summary: Number to power of exponent; return type matches first arg

RAND.summary: Random 0-1 once per statement; NEWID for different per row
RAND.example: SELECT RAND(1)   -- Same seed produces same value every time

ROUND.summary: Round to length digits; nonzero third arg truncates instead

SIGN.summary: 1 for positive, 0 for zero, -1 for negative; NULL stays NULL

SQRT.summary: Square root as float; negative argument fails the statement

CHOOSE.summary: Select value at 1-based index; NULL if out of range

ISNUMERIC.summary: 1 if convertible to any numeric type; currency symbols count

PARSE.summary: Convert string to date/number by culture; uses CLR, slower

TRY_CAST.summary: Like CAST but NULL on failure instead of statement error

TRY_PARSE.summary: Like PARSE but NULL on failure; also uses CLR

APP_NAME.summary: Application name sent by the client; not verified

BINARY_CHECKSUM.summary: Binary checksum, case-sensitive; CHECKSUM follows collation
BINARY_CHECKSUM.example: SELECT BINARY_CHECKSUM('a'), BINARY_CHECKSUM('A')   -- Two different values

CHECKSUM.summary: Checksum per collation; different values may collide
CHECKSUM.example: SELECT CHECKSUM('a'), CHECKSUM('A')   -- Same when collation is case-insensitive

DB_NAME.summary: Database name; omit argument for current database

HOST_NAME.summary: Computer name from client; not guaranteed accurate
HOST_NAME.example: SELECT HOST_NAME()   -- Client machine name sent at connection

IDENT_CURRENT.summary: Last identity value for a table, across sessions and scopes
IDENT_CURRENT.example: SELECT IDENT_CURRENT('dbo.Loan')   -- Includes values inserted by others

NEWID.summary: Random uniqueidentifier; clustered key causes page splits
NEWID.example: SELECT NEWID()   -- Each row different, ORDER BY it for random sort

NEWSEQUENTIALID.summary: Ascending uniqueidentifier; only as a column default
NEWSEQUENTIALID.example: ALTER TABLE dbo.Copy ADD Tag uniqueidentifier DEFAULT NEWSEQUENTIALID()   -- Usage only

OBJECT_ID.summary: object_id, or NULL; used to check whether an object exists
OBJECT_ID.example: SELECT OBJECT_ID('dbo.Loan', 'U')   -- 'U' is table, returns NULL if not found

OBJECT_NAME.summary: Object name from object_id; searches current database

SCHEMA_NAME.summary: Schema name; omit arg for current user's default

SCOPE_IDENTITY.summary: Last identity in this scope; unaffected by triggers
SCOPE_IDENTITY.example: INSERT dbo.Loan (ReaderId) VALUES (1); SELECT SCOPE_IDENTITY()   -- Row inserted

SUSER_SNAME.summary: Login name; omit argument for current connection's login

USER_NAME.summary: Database user name, not the login; login: SUSER_SNAME

ERROR_LINE.summary: Line number of error in CATCH block; returns NULL elsewhere

ERROR_MESSAGE.summary: Full error message in CATCH, with parameters filled in
ERROR_MESSAGE.example: BEGIN TRY SELECT 1/0 END TRY BEGIN CATCH SELECT ERROR_MESSAGE() END CATCH   -- Error text

ERROR_NUMBER.summary: Error number in CATCH block, same value as @@ERROR

ERROR_PROCEDURE.summary: Procedure or trigger that raised the error; NULL if none

ERROR_SEVERITY.summary: Error severity; 11+ enters CATCH, 20+ breaks connection

ERROR_STATE.summary: Error state; tells apart sources of the same error number

ISJSON.summary: 1 if valid JSON; second arg restricts to ARRAY or OBJECT
ISJSON.example: SELECT ISJSON('[1,2]', ARRAY)   -- 1; returns 0 if not an array

JSON_MODIFY.summary: Returns new JSON with a property changed; input unchanged

JSON_QUERY.summary: Extracts object or array; use JSON_VALUE for scalar values

JSON_VALUE.summary: Scalar as nvarchar(4000); objects/arrays use JSON_QUERY

OPENJSON.summary: Table-valued function splitting JSON to rows; 3 cols default
OPENJSON.example: SELECT [key], value FROM OPENJSON('{"a":1}')   -- One row: a, 1

ACOS.summary: Arccosine, argument in range -1 to 1, returns radians

APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT.summary: Distinct count within ~2%; cheaper than COUNT(DISTINCT)
APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT.example: SELECT APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT(CopyNo) FROM dbo.Loan   -- Approximate not exact

ASIN.summary: Arcsine, argument in range -1 to 1, returns radians

ATN2.summary: Two-arg arctangent distinguishes quadrants; ATAN cannot

COL_LENGTH.summary: Column length in bytes; nvarchar is 2x char count

COL_NAME.summary: Column name from object_id and column_id
COL_NAME.example: SELECT COL_NAME(OBJECT_ID('dbo.Loan'), 1)   -- Name of first column

COLUMNPROPERTY.summary: Column property such as IsIdentity, IsComputed

COMPRESS.summary: GZIP-compress to varbinary(max); undo with DECOMPRESS

CONNECTIONPROPERTY.summary: Current connection property such as client_net_address

CONTEXT_INFO.summary: 128 bytes stored by this session via SET CONTEXT_INFO
CONTEXT_INFO.example: SELECT CONTEXT_INFO()   -- NULL if not set

COT.summary: Cotangent in radians; zero causes division by zero error

CRYPT_GEN_RANDOM.summary: Cryptographically strong random bytes, specify length
CRYPT_GEN_RANDOM.example: SELECT CRYPT_GEN_RANDOM(4)   -- 4 bytes of random data

CUME_DIST.summary: Cumulative distribution: share of rows <= current, 0 to 1
CUME_DIST.example: SELECT CUME_DIST() OVER (ORDER BY LoanDate) FROM dbo.Loan   -- Last row is always 1

CURRENT_TIMEZONE_ID.summary: Current server time zone ID for AT TIME ZONE
CURRENT_TIMEZONE_ID.example: SELECT SYSDATETIME() AT TIME ZONE CURRENT_TIMEZONE_ID()   -- Add timezone offset

DATABASE_PRINCIPAL_ID.summary: Database principal ID; omit arg for current user

DATABASEPROPERTYEX.summary: Database property such as Collation, Recovery

DATE_BUCKET.summary: Round time to fixed-width interval start for grouping
DATE_BUCKET.example: SELECT DATE_BUCKET(WEEK, 2, '2026-09-08')   -- Every 2 weeks, returns start of bucket

DATEDIFF_BIG.summary: Like DATEDIFF but returns bigint; nanoseconds won't overflow

DATETIME2FROMPARTS.summary: Assemble datetime2; last arg is fractional second digits

DATETIMEFROMPARTS.summary: Assemble datetime; invalid segment fails statement

DATETIMEOFFSETFROMPARTS.summary: Assemble datetimeoffset; offset as separate hour/minute

DATETRUNC.summary: Truncate date/time to unit; return type matches arg

DB_ID.summary: Database identifier; omit argument for current database
DB_ID.example: SELECT DB_ID()   -- database_id of current database

DECOMPRESS.summary: Undo COMPRESS; returns varbinary(max), CAST back to text

DECRYPTBYPASSPHRASE.summary: Decrypt with a passphrase; wrong one returns NULL, no error

ENCRYPTBYPASSPHRASE.summary: Encrypt with a passphrase to varbinary(8000); keep it safe
ENCRYPTBYPASSPHRASE.example: SELECT ENCRYPTBYPASSPHRASE('key', 'abc')   -- Different result each execution

FORMATMESSAGE.summary: Build a message from a template and args; never raises

GREATEST.summary: Greatest value; NULL ignored. SQL Server 2022+

HAS_PERMS_BY_NAME.summary: Whether current login has specified permission on object

HOST_ID.summary: Client process ID; with HOST_NAME tells connections apart
HOST_ID.example: SELECT HOST_ID()   -- Client application process ID

IDENT_SEED.summary: Identity seed: the value the first row gets

INDEX_COL.summary: Name of column at index key position
INDEX_COL.example: SELECT INDEX_COL('dbo.Loan', 1, 1)   -- First key column of clustered index

INDEXPROPERTY.summary: Index property such as IsClustered, IsUnique

IS_MEMBER.summary: Whether current user is in a database role or Windows group

IS_OBJECTSIGNED.summary: Object signed with specified certificate or asymmetric key

IS_ROLEMEMBER.summary: Whether specified principal is member of database role

IS_SRVROLEMEMBER.summary: Whether specified login is member of server role

JSON_ARRAY.summary: Assembles JSON array string. Available SQL Server 2022+
JSON_ARRAY.example: SELECT JSON_ARRAY(1, 'a', NULL)   -- '[1,"a"]', NULL skipped by default

JSON_OBJECT.summary: Assembles JSON object string. Available SQL Server 2022+
JSON_OBJECT.example: SELECT JSON_OBJECT('a': 1, 'b': NULL)   -- '{"a":1}', NULL skipped by default

JSON_PATH_EXISTS.summary: 1 if the path exists, else 0; SQL Server 2022+

LEAST.summary: Smallest value; NULL ignored. SQL Server 2022+

OBJECT_DEFINITION.summary: Module definition text; NULL if encrypted or denied

OBJECTPROPERTY.summary: Object property such as IsTable, TableHasPrimaryKey

OBJECTPROPERTYEX.summary: Like OBJECTPROPERTY but returns sql_variant; more properties

ORIGINAL_LOGIN.summary: Original login before any EXECUTE AS switch
ORIGINAL_LOGIN.example: SELECT ORIGINAL_LOGIN()   -- Original login even after login switch

PARSENAME.summary: Part of a four-part name; 1 is the rightmost (object name)

PERCENTILE_CONT.summary: Percentile interpolates if between rows; 0.5 is median

PERCENTILE_DISC.summary: Percentile as an actual value, no interpolation

PERCENT_RANK.summary: Relative rank, 0 to 1; first row is always 0
PERCENT_RANK.example: SELECT PERCENT_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY LoanDate) FROM dbo.Loan   -- (rank-1)/(row count-1)

RADIANS.summary: Convert degrees to radians; int arg truncates result

SCHEMA_ID.summary: Schema identifier; omit argument for default schema

SERVERPROPERTY.summary: Instance property such as ProductVersion, Edition

SESSION_CONTEXT.summary: Read value set by session via sp_set_session_context
SESSION_CONTEXT.example: SELECT SESSION_CONTEXT(N'ReaderId')   -- NULL if not set

SMALLDATETIMEFROMPARTS.summary: Assemble smalldatetime; precision to minute only

SQL_VARIANT_PROPERTY.summary: Base type, precision or scale of a sql_variant value

STATS_DATE.example: SELECT STATS_DATE(OBJECT_ID('dbo.Loan'), 1)   -- Statistics update time for first stat

STRING_ESCAPE.summary: Escape special characters; type supports only json

SUSER_ID.summary: Login ID; omit arg for current connection's login
SUSER_ID.example: SELECT SUSER_ID()   -- principal_id of current login

SUSER_NAME.summary: Login name from login identifier; SUSER_SNAME takes SID

SUSER_SID.summary: Login SID; omit argument for current connection's login

TIMEFROMPARTS.summary: Assemble time; last arg is fractional second digits

TYPE_ID.summary: Type identifier; returns NULL if not found

TYPEPROPERTY.summary: Type property such as Precision, Scale, AllowsNull

USER_ID.summary: Database user identifier; omit argument for current user

XACT_STATE.summary: 1 can commit, -1 rollback only, 0 no transaction
XACT_STATE.example: IF XACT_STATE() = -1 ROLLBACK TRANSACTION   -- Check this first in CATCH block

NOLOCK.example: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM dbo.Loan WITH (NOLOCK)   -- Row may appear/disappear

READPAST.example: SELECT TOP (1) CopyNo FROM dbo.Copy WITH (READPAST, UPDLOCK)   -- Get one unlocked row

UPDLOCK.example: SELECT CopyNo FROM dbo.Copy WITH (UPDLOCK) WHERE CopyNo = 1   -- Lock row before update

INDEX.example: SELECT * FROM dbo.Loan WITH (INDEX(IX_Loan_ReaderId))   -- Name or number

RECOMPILE.example: SELECT * FROM dbo.Loan WHERE ReaderId = @readerId OPTION (RECOMPILE)   -- Plan not cached

MAXDOP.example: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM dbo.LoanDetail OPTION (MAXDOP 1)   -- 0 uses config

@@ROWCOUNT.example: UPDATE dbo.Loan SET LoanDate = SYSDATETIME(); SELECT @@ROWCOUNT   -- Next overwrites

@@ERROR.example: IF @@ERROR <> 0 ROLLBACK TRANSACTION   -- Previous stmt only; use TRY

@@IDENTITY.example: INSERT dbo.Loan (ReaderId) VALUES (1); SELECT SCOPE_IDENTITY()   -- Triggers mislead

@@TRANCOUNT.example: BEGIN TRANSACTION; SELECT @@TRANCOUNT   -- Nested only outer commits

@@FETCH_STATUS.example: WHILE @@FETCH_STATUS = 0 FETCH NEXT FROM copies INTO @copyNo   -- 0 success
